name: John Wayne
hook: The Duke, whose Westerns and war films Jeopardy returns to for True Grit and Stagecoach.

facts.label: 142 leading roles
facts.statement: John Wayne played 142 leading roles, a Guinness record, and turned down the role of Dirty Harry.

facts.label: Rooster Cogburn
facts.statement: Wayne won his only Oscar for True Grit (1969) as Rooster Cogburn, the one-eyed marshal; he returned to the role in 1975's Rooster Cogburn.

facts.label: Stagecoach
facts.statement: Stagecoach (1939), John Ford's Western named for a vehicle, made Wayne a star.

facts.label: John Ford
facts.statement: Ford directed Wayne in many films, including Fort Apache, Rio Grande, and finally Donovan's Reef in 1963.

facts.label: The Searchers
facts.statement: The Searchers (1956) is Ford's masterpiece, with Wayne searching for his niece; its line "That'll be the day" inspired Buddy Holly.

facts.label: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
facts.statement: In The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance (1962) Jimmy Stewart returns to Shinbone for Wayne's funeral; Burt and Hal wrote a song of the same name.
associations: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance

facts.label: The Green Berets
facts.statement: The Green Berets (1968) was Wayne's Vietnam War film; Richard Pryor had a small part.
